title: Official blog workflow runbook stage 17
summary: This iteration adds an operator runbook for the official-blog knowledge workflow. It sequences preview feed parsing, preview-only intake, AI review packet creation, AI decision normalization, human authoring, reviewed-authoring validation, author-record dry-run, final curated-record writes, and separate public projection validation.

lessons.lesson: The official-blog ingestion path needs an explicit operator sequence after the CLI stages exist.
lessons.evidence: Stage 17 adds `tasks/official-blog-workflow-runbook.md` with ordered commands from `official-blog:parse-feed` through final `official-blog:author-records` writes.
lessons.recommended_action: Use the runbook when adding new OpenAI or Anthropic official-blog records.

lessons.lesson: The user-approved admission standard should remain visible at operation time, not only in code tests.
lessons.evidence: The runbook documents include/exclude rules for product, model, engineering-practice, harness, and multi-agent workflow posts while excluding ordinary partnerships and customer adoption news.
lessons.recommended_action: Review every new candidate against the runbook admission standard before authoring.

suggestions.issue: The workflow still relies on manually prepared feed/export and AI decision artifacts.
suggestions.evidence: The runbook intentionally sequences local CLI steps but does not add a single orchestrating command.
suggestions.suggestion: Add fixture-backed examples for one OpenAI and one Anthropic end-to-end run before introducing orchestration.
suggestions.expected_benefit: Examples will make the runbook easier to execute and give future orchestration a stable contract.
suggestions.promotion_path: Future project iteration with tests that replay local fixtures.
validation_evidence: official blog workflow runbook is executable and safety-backed

followups.action: Add local fixture-backed OpenAI and Anthropic examples that exercise the complete runbook without live network access.
After fixture examples are stable, consider a single orchestrator command that calls the runbook steps with explicit checkpoints.
